title.en: Volume 293 Biographies 80: Li Fu, Cai Ting, Xie Jishi, Chen Xuehai
title.raw: 卷293 列傳八十 李绂 蔡珽 谢济世 陈学海

sentences.zh: 列傳八十

translations.literal: Biographies 80
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 80

sentences.zh: 李紱蔡珽謝濟世陳學海

translations.literal: Li Fu, Cai Ting, Xie Jishi, Chen Xuehai
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu, Cai Ting, Xie Jishi, and Chen Xuehai

sentences.zh: 李紱，字巨來，江西臨川人。

translations.literal: Li Fu, styled Julai, was a man of Linchuan in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu, whose style name was Julai, came from Linchuan in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，好學，讀書經目成誦。

translations.literal: In youth he was orphaned and poor, loved learning, and upon reading a text once could recite it from memory.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young and poor, he loved study and could recite a text after a single reading.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十八年，成進士，改庶吉士，散館授編修。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year of Kangxi he became a jinshi, was made a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and upon leaving the academy was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year of the Kangxi reign he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and after leaving the academy was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍講學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to lecturer in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in due course to the post of lecturer in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，擢內閣學士，尋遷左副都御史，仍兼學士。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician, and soon after transferred to left vice censor-in-chief while still holding the academician title.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year he was made a Grand Secretariat academician and soon after transferred to left vice censor-in-chief, retaining his academician rank as well.

sentences.zh: 六十年，充會試副考官。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he served as associate examiner for the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year he served as associate examiner for the metropolitan civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 出榜日，黃霧風霾，上語大學士等曰：「此榜或有亂臣賊子，否亦當有讀書積學之士不得中式，怨氣所致。

translations.literal: On the day the list was published, yellow fog and wind-borne haze appeared. The emperor said to the grand secretaries and others: 'This list may contain traitors and villains; if not, there must be scholars of long study who failed to pass, and resentful qi has caused this.'
translations.idiomatic: On the day the results were posted, yellow fog and murky winds arose. The emperor told the grand secretaries and others, "This cohort may harbor traitors and villains—or else men of deep learning have been passed over, and their resentment has brought this on."

sentences.zh: 」命磨勘試卷，劣者停殿試。

translations.literal: ' He ordered a re-examination of the papers; the inferior were barred from the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the papers reviewed again, and those judged inferior were barred from the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 又賜滿洲舉人留保、直隸舉人王蘭生進士。

translations.literal: He also granted jinshi status to the Manchu provincial graduate Liubao and the Zhili provincial graduate Wang Lansheng.
translations.idiomatic: He also conferred jinshi degrees on the Manchu provincial graduate Liubao and the Zhili provincial graduate Wang Lansheng.

sentences.zh: 下第舉子群聚紱門，投瓦石喧閧。

translations.literal: Failed candidates gathered in a mob at Fu's gate, throwing tiles and stones in a noisy uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates who had failed gathered at Fu's gate, hurling tiles and stones in a noisy riot.

sentences.zh: 御史舒庫疏劾，下部議，責紱匿不奏，奪官，發永定河工效力。

translations.literal: Censor Shuku memorialized in impeachment. The matter was referred to the ministry for deliberation; Fu was charged with concealing the affair and not reporting it, stripped of office, and sent to labor on the Yongding River works.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Shuku impeached him in a memorial. After deliberation at the ministry, Fu was found to have concealed the affair and failed to report it; he was dismissed and sent to serve on the Yongding River project.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，特命复官，署吏部侍郎，赴山東催漕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was specially ordered restored to office, acting vice minister of personnel, and sent to Shandong to press grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongzheng reign he was specially restored to office as acting vice minister of personnel and sent to Shandong to expedite the grain transport.

sentences.zh: 尋授兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 上令截留湖南等省漕糧於天津收貯，旋又命估價出糶。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered grain transport from Hunan and other provinces detained and stored at Tianjin, and soon after ordered it sold at appraised price.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered grain transport from Hunan and other provinces held at Tianjin for storage, and soon afterward ordered it sold off at appraised prices.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，授廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year he was appointed governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year he was appointed governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「廣西賀縣大金、蕉木二山產礦砂，五十里外為廣東梅峒汛，又數里為宿塘寨，礦徒盤據，時時竊發。

translations.literal: He memorialized: 'In Guangxi, He County's Dajin and Jiaomu mountains produce ore sand. Fifty li beyond lies the Guangdong Meidong garrison post, and a few li farther is Sutang Stockade. Miners occupy the area and from time to time rise in secret disturbances.'
translations.idiomatic: He reported, "In He County, Guangxi, the Dajin and Jiaomu mountains yield ore sand. Fifty li away lies the Meidong garrison of Guangdong, and a few li beyond that is Sutang Stockade, where miners have entrenched themselves and periodically stir up trouble."

sentences.zh: 臣方擬嚴禁，聞總督孔毓珣條陳開採，因而中止。

translations.literal: Your servant was about to impose strict prohibition when he heard that Governor-General Kong Yuxun had memorialized proposing to open mining, and therefore suspended action.
translations.idiomatic: I was preparing to enforce a strict ban when I learned that Governor-General Kong Yuxun had memorialized proposing to open the mines, and I therefore held off.

sentences.zh: 將來或恐滋事。

translations.literal: In the future there may be fear of causing incidents.
translations.idiomatic: This may lead to trouble later on.

sentences.zh: 」毓珣奏同時至，廷議寢其事。

translations.literal: ' Yuxun's memorial arrived at the same time, and court deliberation shelved the matter.
translations.idiomatic: " Kong Yuxun's memorial arrived at the same time, and after court deliberation the matter was shelved.

sentences.zh: 上命以諭毓珣者示紱，令協力禁止。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that what had been told Yuxun be shown to Fu and that they cooperate in prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that the instructions given to Kong Yuxun be shown to Fu and that the two cooperate in enforcing the ban.

sentences.zh: 紱疏陳練兵，列舉嚴賞罰、演陣法、習用槍砲、豫備帳房鑼鍋諸事，上嘉其留心武備。

translations.literal: Fu memorialized on drilling troops, listing strict rewards and punishments, practicing battle formations, training in firearms, and preparing tents, gongs, and cooking pots, among other matters. The emperor praised his attention to military preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: Fu memorialized on troop training, citing strict rewards and punishments, drill in battle formations, practice with firearms, and the provision of tents, gongs, and cooking pots, among other measures. The emperor commended his attention to military readiness.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，巡撫陳元龍奏請開捐，都計收穀百十七萬石有奇，石折銀一兩一錢，而發州縣買穀石止三錢，不足以糴。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi period, Governor Chen Yuanlong memorialized requesting to open sale of offices; in all more than 1,170,000 shi of grain were collected, each shi converted at 1 tael 1 mace of silver, yet what was issued to prefectures and counties to purchase grain was only 3 mace per shi—insufficient to buy grain.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign, Governor Chen Yuanlong had memorialized to open the sale of offices; in all more than 1,170,000 shi of grain were collected, valued at 1 tael 1 mace of silver per shi, yet prefectures and counties were given only 3 mace per shi to purchase grain—far too little to buy it.

sentences.zh: 至紱上官，尚虧四萬餘石，紱奏請限一月補足。

translations.literal: By the time Fu took office there was still a shortfall of more than 40,000 shi. Fu memorialized requesting a one-month limit to make it up.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu took office, more than 40,000 shi were still outstanding. He memorialized asking for one month to make up the deficit.

sentences.zh: 會提督韓良輔條奏墾荒，下紱議，紱請以桂林、柳州、梧州、南寧四府收貯捐穀動支為開墾費。

translations.literal: At the same time Regional Commander Han Liangfu memorialized on opening wasteland for cultivation; the matter was referred to Fu for deliberation. Fu requested that stored contribution grain from the four prefectures of Guilin, Liuzhou, Wuzhou, and Nanning be expended as opening-cultivation funds.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Regional Commander Han Liangfu memorialized on reclaiming wasteland, and the matter was referred to Fu. Fu proposed drawing on stored contribution grain from the prefectures of Guilin, Liuzhou, Wuzhou, and Nanning to fund the reclamation.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕觀紱意，不過借開墾以銷捐穀。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'I see Fu's intent is merely to use opening cultivation to write off contribution grain.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I see that Fu's aim is simply to use land reclamation to write off the contribution grain."

sentences.zh: 當時陳元龍等首尾不清，朕知之甚詳。

translations.literal: At the time Chen Yuanlong and others were unclear from start to finish; I know this in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuanlong and the others handled the matter incoherently from start to finish—I know the details very well."

sentences.zh: 應令元龍等往廣西料理。

translations.literal: Yuanlong and others should be ordered to go to Guangxi to handle it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlong and the others should be sent to Guangxi to sort it out."

sentences.zh: 」並諭紱詳察，毋隱諱瞻徇，自承虧空。

translations.literal: ' He also instructed Fu to investigate thoroughly, not to conceal or show favoritism, and not to take the shortfall upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: " He also instructed Fu to investigate thoroughly, neither concealing facts nor showing favoritism, and not to shoulder the deficit himself.

sentences.zh: 尋紱奏察出督撫、司道、府廳分得羨餘銀八十二萬有奇，勒限分償，上嘉紱秉公執正。

translations.literal: Soon after Fu memorialized that investigation had revealed governors, provincial commissioners, and prefectural officials had shared surplus silver of more than 820,000 taels; they were ordered to repay within a set limit. The emperor praised Fu for upholding justice impartially.
translations.idiomatic: Fu soon reported that his investigation had uncovered more than 820,000 taels of surplus silver divided among governors, provincial commissioners, and prefectural officials, and he ordered them to repay within a fixed deadline. The emperor praised Fu for acting impartially and with integrity.

sentences.zh: 紱在吏部時，年羹堯子富等捐造營房，下部議敘，不肯從優，為羹堯所嫉；

translations.literal: When Fu was at the Ministry of Personnel, Nian Gengyao's son Fu and others made contributions to build barracks; the matter was referred to the ministry for deliberation on rewards, and he refused to grant preferential treatment, incurring Gengyao's resentment;
translations.idiomatic: While Fu served at the Ministry of Personnel, Nian Gengyao's son Fu and others had contributed funds to build barracks. When the ministry deliberated on rewards, Fu refused to grant them preferential treatment, and Nian Gengyao came to resent him;

sentences.zh: 及上命天津截漕估糶盈餘銀五千交守道桑成鼎貯庫，紱至廣西，成鼎使齎以畀紱。

translations.literal: When the emperor ordered that the surplus of 5,000 taels from appraised sale of detained grain transport at Tianjin be handed to Circuit Intendant Sang Chengdian for storage, Fu went to Guangxi and Chengdian had it delivered to Fu.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ordered that 5,000 taels of surplus from the appraised sale of grain detained at Tianjin be placed in the custody of Circuit Intendant Sang Chengdian, Fu went to Guangxi and Chengdian had the sum delivered to him.

sentences.zh: 紱具摺送直隸巡撫李維鈞會奏。

translations.literal: Fu prepared a memorial and sent it to Zhili Governor Li Weijun for joint memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Fu prepared a memorial and forwarded it to Zhili Governor Li Weijun for a joint report.

sentences.zh: 維鈞匿不上，紱乃奏聞。

translations.literal: Weijun concealed it and did not submit it; Fu then memorialized directly.
translations.idiomatic: Li Weijun withheld it and did not submit it, so Fu reported the matter directly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 先是，羹堯朝京師，入對，舉此訐紱，謂紱乾沒。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gengyao came to the capital for audience, he cited this to denounce Fu, saying Fu had embezzled.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Nian Gengyao came to the capital for audience, he had cited this matter to denounce Fu, accusing him of embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 上以問維鈞，維鈞言紱取數百金治裝，餘尚貯庫。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Weijun; Weijun said Fu had taken several hundred taels for travel expenses and the rest was still in the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Li Weijun, who said Fu had taken several hundred taels for travel expenses while the rest remained in the treasury.

sentences.zh: 紱奏至，上謂維鈞與羹堯比，欲陷紱。

translations.literal: When Fu's memorial arrived, the emperor said Weijun was in league with Gengyao and wished to frame Fu.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu's memorial arrived, the emperor concluded that Li Weijun was in league with Nian Gengyao and meant to frame Fu.

sentences.zh: 諭獎紱，命留充公用。

translations.literal: He issued instructions commending Fu and ordered the funds retained for public use.
translations.idiomatic: He commended Fu and ordered the funds retained for public use.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，紱奏言：「太平、思恩府界流言安南內亂。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year Fu memorialized: 'On the border of Taiping and Si'en prefectures there are rumors of internal disorder in Annam.'
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year Fu reported, "Rumors of civil strife in Annam have spread along the border between Taiping and Si'en prefectures."

sentences.zh: 有潘騰龍者，自言為莫姓後，其黨黃把勢、陳亂彈等煽誘為亂。

translations.literal: There is one Pan Tenglong who claims to be a descendant of the Mo clan; his followers Huang Bashishi, Chen Luandan, and others incite and entice people to rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Pan Tenglong claims descent from the Mo clan, and his followers Huang Bashishi, Chen Luandan, and others are stirring people to revolt.

sentences.zh: 嚴飭將吏捕治。

translations.literal: Strict orders have been issued to generals and officials to arrest and punish them.
translations.idiomatic: I have strictly ordered the military and civil officers to arrest and punish them."

sentences.zh: 」上諭曰：「封疆之內，宜整理振作。

translations.literal: ' The emperor instructed: 'Within the frontier, one should put things in order and rouse effort.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied, "Within our borders affairs should be put in order and vigor restored.

sentences.zh: 至於安邊柔遠，最忌貪利圖功，當慎之又慎！

translations.literal: As for securing the borders and pacifying distant peoples, what is most to be feared is greed for profit and seeking merit—one must be cautious again and again!'
translations.idiomatic: In securing the borders and pacifying distant peoples, nothing is more dangerous than greed for profit or a thirst for glory—be doubly cautious!"

sentences.zh: 」九月，奏：「瑤、僮頑梗，修仁十排、天河三甿為尤甚，常出劫掠。

translations.literal: ' In the ninth month he memorialized: 'The Yao and Zhuang are obstinate; the Ten Pai of Xiuren and the Three Villages of Tianhe are especially severe and often go out raiding.'
translations.idiomatic: " In the ninth month he reported, "The Yao and Zhuang are obstinate; the Ten Pai of Xiuren and the Three Villages of Tianhe are the worst offenders and frequently raid neighboring areas."

sentences.zh: 臣遣吏入十排，捕得其渠。

translations.literal: Your servant sent officials into the Ten Pai and captured their ringleader.
translations.idiomatic: I sent officials into the Ten Pai and captured their leader.

sentences.zh: 三甿阻萬山中，所種田在隘外。

translations.literal: The Three Villages are blocked in ten-thousand-fold mountains; their fields lie beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Villages lie deep in rugged mountains, with their fields planted beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 臣發兵守隘，斷其收穫。

translations.literal: Your servant dispatched troops to guard the passes and cut off their harvest.
translations.idiomatic: I sent troops to hold the passes and cut off their harvest.

sentences.zh: 其渠今亦出自歸。

translations.literal: Their ringleader has now also come out and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Their leader has now come out and surrendered as well."

sentences.zh: 」上獎其辦理得宜。

translations.literal: ' The emperor commended his handling as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor commended his handling of the matter.

sentences.zh: 旋授直隸總督。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed governor-general of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor-general of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 四年，紱入覲。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Fu came to court for audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Fu came to court for audience.

sentences.zh: 初，左都御史蔡珽薦起其故吏知縣黃振國授河南信陽知州，忤巡撫田文鏡。

translations.literal: Earlier, Left Censor-in-Chief Cai Ting had recommended his former subordinate, Magistrate Huang Zhenguo, for appointment as prefect of Xinyang in Henan, offending Governor Tian Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Left Censor-in-Chief Cai Ting had recommended his former subordinate Magistrate Huang Zhenguo for appointment as prefect of Xinyang in Henan, which offended Governor Tian Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 文鏡馭吏嚴，尤惡科目，劾振國貪劣。

translations.literal: Wenjing governed subordinates strictly and especially hated examination-degree holders; he impeached Zhenguo for greed and misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing ruled his subordinates harshly and especially despised men who had risen through the civil service examinations; he impeached Zhenguo for corruption and misconduct.

sentences.zh: 紱過河南，詰文鏡胡為有意蹂踐士人。

translations.literal: When Fu passed through Henan he questioned Wenjing: why deliberately trample upon scholars?
translations.idiomatic: When Fu passed through Henan he confronted Wenjing, asking why he deliberately abused men of learning.

sentences.zh: 入對，因極言文鏡貪虐，且謂文鏡所劾屬吏，如振國及邵言綸、汪諴皆枉，振國已死獄中。

translations.literal: At audience he spoke at length of Wenjing's greed and cruelty, and said that subordinates Wenjing had impeached, such as Zhenguo, Shao Yanlun, and Wang Yan, were all wronged, and Zhenguo had already died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he spoke at length of Wenjing's greed and cruelty, and said that subordinates Wenjing had impeached—among them Zhenguo, Shao Yanlun, and Wang Yan—had all been wronged, and that Zhenguo had already died in prison.

sentences.zh: 文鏡因紱語，先密疏聞，謂紱與振國同年袒護。

translations.literal: Because of Fu's words, Wenjing first sent a secret memorial, saying Fu and Zhenguo were examination cohort-mates and Fu was showing favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Fu's remarks, Wenjing sent a secret memorial first, claiming that Fu and Zhenguo were examination cohort-mates and that Fu was shielding him.

sentences.zh: 紱疏辨，上不直紱，而振國實未死，逮至京師，上更謂紱妄語。

translations.literal: Fu memorialized in defense; the emperor did not side with Fu. Zhenguo had in fact not died; when he was brought to the capital, the emperor further said Fu had spoken falsely.
translations.idiomatic: Fu memorialized in his own defense, but the emperor did not take his side. Zhenguo had in fact not died; when he was brought to the capital, the emperor concluded that Fu had lied.

sentences.zh: 良輔奏雲南、廣西所屬土司與貴州接壤者，皆改歸貴州安籠鎮節制，命紱往與雲貴總督高其倬會勘，疏請循舊制，從之。

translations.literal: Liangfu memorialized that native chieftains subordinate to Yunnan and Guangxi bordering Guizhou should all be placed under the control of Guizhou's Anlong garrison; the emperor ordered Fu to go and jointly survey with Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Gao Qizhuo. Fu memorialized requesting to follow the old system, and it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Liangfu had memorialized that native chieftains under Yunnan and Guangxi bordering Guizhou should all be placed under the Anlong garrison of Guizhou. The emperor ordered Fu to go and conduct a joint survey with Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Gao Qizhuo. Fu memorialized asking to follow the old arrangements, and his request was approved.

sentences.zh: 紱還直隸，時上譴責諸弟允禩、允禟等，更允禟名塞思黑，幽諸西寧，复移置保定，命胡什禮監送。

translations.literal: Fu returned to Zhili. At the time the emperor was reprimanding his brothers Yinsi, Yintang, and others; he changed Yintang's name to Seshei and confined him at Xining, then moved him to Baoding, ordering Hushili to supervise the transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Fu returned to Zhili. At that time the emperor was censuring his brothers Yinsi, Yintang, and others; he changed Yintang's name to Seshei, confined him at Xining, then moved him to Baoding and ordered Hushili to supervise the transfer.

sentences.zh: 紱語胡什禮：「塞思黑至，當便宜行事。

translations.literal: Fu told Hushili: 'When Seshei arrives, act as circumstances require.'
translations.idiomatic: Fu told Hushili, "When Seshei arrives, act as circumstances require."

sentences.zh: 」胡什禮以聞，上以為不可，命諭紱，紱奏初無此語。

translations.literal: ' Hushili reported this; the emperor deemed it unacceptable and ordered Fu informed. Fu memorialized that he had never said such words.
translations.idiomatic: Hushili reported this to the throne. The emperor found it unacceptable and ordered Fu informed. Fu memorialized that he had never said such a thing.

sentences.zh: 塞思黑至保定，未幾，紱以病聞，尋遂死。

translations.literal: Seshei arrived at Baoding; before long Fu reported illness, and soon afterward died.
translations.idiomatic: Seshei arrived at Baoding; before long Fu reported that he was ill, and soon afterward he died.

sentences.zh: 是冬，御史謝濟世劾文鏡貪虐，仍及誣劾振國等。

translations.literal: That winter, Censor Xie Jishi impeached Wenjing for greed and cruelty, again citing the false impeachment of Zhenguo and others.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, Censor Xie Jishi impeached Wenjing for greed and cruelty, again citing the wrongful impeachment of Zhenguo and the others.

sentences.zh: 上奪濟世官，下大學士九卿會鞫，戍濟世阿爾泰軍前。

translations.literal: The emperor stripped Jishi of office, referred the case to the grand secretaries and Nine Chief Ministers for joint trial, and banished Jishi to serve before the army in Altai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stripped Xie Jishi of office, referred the case to the grand secretaries and Nine Chief Ministers for joint trial, and banished him to serve before the army in Altai.

sentences.zh: 上以濟世奏與紱語同，疑紱與為黨，召紱授工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Because Jishi's memorial matched Fu's words, the emperor suspected Fu was in league with him and summoned Fu, appointing him vice minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xie Jishi's memorial echoed Fu's earlier words, the emperor suspected Fu was in league with him and summoned Fu, appointing him vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 紱在廣西捕亂苗莫東旺置天河縣獄，獄未竟，紱移督直隸去。

translations.literal: While in Guangxi Fu had captured the rebellious Miao Mo Dongwang and placed him in Tianhe County prison; the case was not concluded when Fu was transferred to govern Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: While in Guangxi Fu had captured the rebellious Miao leader Mo Dongwang and placed him in Tianhe County prison. The case was unfinished when Fu was transferred to govern Zhili.

sentences.zh: 久之，蠻、僮集眾破獄，劫東旺去。

translations.literal: After a long time, Man and Zhuang gathered a crowd, broke the prison, and carried Dongwang off.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward, Man and Zhuang tribesmen gathered in force, broke open the prison, and carried Dongwang away.

sentences.zh: 五年春，良輔署廣西巡撫，奏聞。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, Liangfu acting as governor of Guangxi memorialized to inform the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year, Liangfu, acting as governor of Guangxi, reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上以詰紱，下部察議。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Fu and referred the matter to the ministry for investigation and deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Fu and referred the matter to the ministry for investigation.

sentences.zh: 會都察院奏廣西州判程旦詣院訴土司羅文剛掠村落抗官兵，上責紱與繼任巡撫甘汝來逡巡貽害，命紱與汝來至廣西捕治，不獲，當重譴。

translations.literal: At the same time the Censorate memorialized that Guangxi Assistant Prefect Cheng Dan had come to the court to complain that native chieftain Luo Wengang had raided villages and resisted government troops. The emperor blamed Fu and his successor Governor Gan Rulai for hesitation that had caused harm, and ordered Fu and Rulai to go to Guangxi to arrest and punish them; if they failed, severe punishment would follow.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Censorate reported that Guangxi Assistant Prefect Cheng Dan had come to the court to complain that native chieftain Luo Wengang had raided villages and resisted government troops. The emperor blamed Fu and his successor Governor Gan Rulai for dithering that had allowed the harm, and ordered Fu and Rulai to go to Guangxi to capture and punish the offenders; if they failed, they would face severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 紱至廣西，東旺聞而自歸，文剛亦捕得。

translations.literal: When Fu reached Guangxi, Dongwang heard and submitted of his own accord; Wengang was also captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu reached Guangxi, Dongwang heard of his arrival and surrendered of his own accord, and Wengang was captured as well.

sentences.zh: 直隸總督宜兆熊劾知府曾逢聖、知縣王遊虧空錢糧，上以逢聖、遊皆紱所薦，命詰紱。

translations.literal: Zhili Governor-General Yi Zhaoxiong impeached Prefect Zeng Fengsheng and Magistrate Wang You for deficits in tax grain. Because Fengsheng and You were both recommended by Fu, the emperor ordered Fu questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili Governor-General Yi Zhaoxiong impeached Prefect Zeng Fengsheng and Magistrate Wang You for deficits in tax grain. Because both men had been recommended by Fu, the emperor ordered Fu questioned.

sentences.zh: 戶部議覆，紱在直隸奏報懷來倉圮，穀為小民竊食，當下直隸總督詳察。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue deliberated and replied: Fu, while in Zhili, had memorialized that the Huailai granary had collapsed and grain was stolen and eaten by common people; the Zhili governor-general should be ordered to investigate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue deliberated and replied that while in Zhili Fu had reported the collapse of the Huailai granary and claimed the grain had been stolen and eaten by commoners; the Zhili governor-general should be ordered to investigate in detail.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「穀至六千餘石，豈能竊食至盡？

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Grain amounting to more than 6,000 shi—how could it be stolen and eaten to the last grain?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "More than 6,000 shi of grain—how could commoners have stolen and eaten it all?"

sentences.zh: 明系紱市恩，為縣吏脫罪。

translations.literal: Clearly Fu was currying favor and securing release from guilt for county officials.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly Fu was currying favor and shielding the county officials from punishment.

sentences.zh: 當責紱償補，以成其市恩。

translations.literal: Fu should be charged to make restitution, to complete his currying of favor.
translations.idiomatic: Fu should be made to make restitution himself, to complete his act of favor-seeking."

sentences.zh: 」兆熊又劾知縣李先枝私派累民，上以先枝亦紱所薦，責紱欺罔，奪官；

translations.literal: ' Zhaoxiong again impeached Magistrate Li Xianzhi for unauthorized levies burdening the people. Because Xianzhi was also recommended by Fu, the emperor charged Fu with deception, stripped him of office;
translations.idiomatic: Yi Zhaoxiong also impeached Magistrate Li Xianzhi for unauthorized levies that burdened the people. Because Li Xianzhi had also been recommended by Fu, the emperor charged Fu with deception and dismissed him;

sentences.zh: 下刑部、議政大臣等會鞫，紱罪凡二十一事，當斬。

translations.literal: the case was referred to the Ministry of Punishments, deliberating ministers, and others for joint trial; Fu's offenses numbered twenty-one in all, warranting execution.
translations.idiomatic: the case was referred to the Ministry of Punishments and the deliberating ministers for joint trial. Fu was found guilty on twenty-one counts, for which the penalty was death.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「紱既知悔過，情詞懇切，且其學問尚優，命免死，纂修八旗通志效力。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: 'Fu has shown he knows repentance; his words are earnest, and his learning is still superior. He is ordered spared death and to serve compiling the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Eight Banners.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ruled, "Fu has shown repentance and his words are earnest; moreover, his learning is still considerable. He is spared death and ordered to serve on the compilation of the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Eight Banners."

sentences.zh: 七年，又以順承郡王錫保奏濟世在阿爾泰供言劾文鏡實受紱及珽指，下紱等刑部。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, because Prince of Shuncheng Xibao memorialized that Jishi, while serving in Altai, had testified that his impeachment of Wenjing was actually at the direction of Fu and Ting, Fu and others were referred to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Prince of Shuncheng Xibao memorialized that while serving in Altai, Xie Jishi had testified that his impeachment of Wenjing had actually been directed by Fu and Cai Ting. Fu and the others were referred to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 會曾靜、張熙獄起，上召王大臣宣諭，並命紱入，諭曰：「朕在籓邸，初不知珽、紱姓名。

translations.literal: At the time the Zeng Jing and Zhang Xi case arose; the emperor summoned princes and ministers to announce instructions and also ordered Fu to enter. He instructed: 'When I was at the princely residence I initially did not know the names of Ting and Fu.'
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Zeng Jing and Zhang Xi case arose. The emperor summoned the princes and ministers to announce his instructions and also ordered Fu to attend. He said, "When I was still at my princely residence I did not even know Ting's and Fu's names."

sentences.zh: 有馬爾濟哈者，能醫。

translations.literal: There was one Ma'erjiha who could practice medicine.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Ma'erjiha who practiced medicine.

sentences.zh: 朕問：'更有能醫者否？

translations.literal: I asked: 'Are there others who can practice medicine?'
translations.idiomatic: I asked, 'Is there anyone else who practices medicine?'

sentences.zh: '以珽對。

translations.literal: He answered with Ting.
translations.idiomatic: He named Ting.

sentences.zh: 召珽來見，珽謂不當與諸王往來，辭不至，以是朕重之。

translations.literal: I summoned Ting to come for an audience; Ting said one should not associate with princes and declined to come. For this I esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: I summoned Ting to an audience, but he said one should not associate with princes and declined to come. For that I held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 年羹堯來京，​​亟稱珽，朕告以嘗招之不來，羹堯以語珽，珽复辭不至，以是朕益重之。

translations.literal: When Nian Gengyao came to the capital he repeatedly praised Ting. I told him I had once summoned Ting and he did not come; Gengyao spoke to Ting, and Ting again declined to come. For this I esteemed him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Nian Gengyao came to the capital he repeatedly praised Ting. I told him I had once summoned Ting and he had not come; Gengyao relayed this to Ting, and Ting again declined. For that I esteemed him all the more.

sentences.zh: 及出為四川巡撫，詣熱河行在，始與相見，為朕言李紱。

translations.literal: When he went out as governor of Sichuan he came to the imperial camp at Rehe and only then met me in person; he spoke to me of Li Fu.
translations.idiomatic: When he went out as governor of Sichuan he came to the imperial camp at Rehe, and only then did we meet in person; he spoke to me of Li Fu.

sentences.zh: 朕知紱自此始。

translations.literal: I came to know of Fu from this point.
translations.idiomatic: That was how I first came to know of Fu.

sentences.zh: 既即位，延訪人才，起紱原官。

translations.literal: After I ascended the throne I sought out talent and restored Fu to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After I ascended the throne I sought out talent and restored Fu to his former office.

sentences.zh: 旋自侍郎出撫廣西，至為直隸總督，徇私廢公，沽名邀譽，致吏治廢弛，人心玩愒。

translations.literal: Soon after he went from vice minister to govern Guangxi, and ultimately became governor-general of Zhili, showing favoritism and neglecting public duty, currying reputation and seeking praise, causing administration to lapse and hearts to grow lax.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went from vice minister to govern Guangxi and ultimately became governor-general of Zhili, yet he showed favoritism, neglected public duty, curried reputation, and sought praise, until administration grew lax and public morale slackened.

sentences.zh: 又如塞思黑自西大通調回，令暫住保定。

translations.literal: Again, when Seshei was transferred back from Xidatong he was ordered to stay temporarily at Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Again, when Seshei was transferred back from Xidatong he was ordered to stay temporarily at Baoding.

sentences.zh: 未幾，紱奏言遘病，不數​​日即死。

translations.literal: Before long Fu memorialized that he had fallen ill; within a few days he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Fu reported that he had fallen ill; within a few days he was dead.

sentences.zh: 奸黨遂謂朕授意於紱，使之戕害。

translations.literal: Wicked partisans then said I had instructed Fu to harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked partisans then claimed I had instructed Fu to harm him.

sentences.zh: 今紱在此，試問朕嘗授意否乎？

translations.literal: Now Fu is here—try asking whether I ever gave such instruction!
translations.idiomatic: Fu is here now—ask him whether I ever gave such an instruction!

sentences.zh: 塞思黑罪本無可赦，豈料其遽死？

translations.literal: Seshei's crimes were originally beyond pardon—who expected he would die so suddenly?
translations.idiomatic: Seshei's crimes were beyond pardon in the first place—who expected him to die so suddenly?

sentences.zh: 紱不將其病死明白於眾，致生疑議，紱能辭其過乎？

translations.literal: Fu did not make clear to the public that he died of illness, giving rise to suspicion—can Fu escape blame for this?
translations.idiomatic: Fu failed to make clear to the public that Seshei had died of illness, giving rise to suspicion—can Fu escape blame for that?

sentences.zh: 田文鏡公忠，而紱與珽極力陷害，使濟世誣劾，必欲遂其私怨。

translations.literal: Tian Wenjing was loyal and devoted, yet Fu and Ting strove to frame him, making Jishi lodge false impeachment, determined to satisfy their private resentments.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Wenjing was loyal and devoted, yet Fu and Ting strove to frame him, having Xie Jishi lodge false charges, all to satisfy their private grudges.

sentences.zh: 此風何可長也？

translations.literal: How can such a practice be allowed to grow?
translations.idiomatic: How can such conduct be tolerated?

sentences.zh: 」復下紱刑部嚴鞫，獄上，請治罪，上寬之。

translations.literal: ' The case was again referred to the Ministry of Punishments for strict interrogation; when the trial concluded they requested punishment, but the emperor showed leniency.
translations.idiomatic: " The case was again referred to the Ministry of Punishments for strict interrogation. When the trial concluded they recommended punishment, but the emperor showed leniency.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，賜侍郎銜，管戶部三庫，尋授戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Gaozong ascended the throne, Fu was granted vice minister rank, placed in charge of the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue, and soon appointed vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianlong Emperor ascended the throne, Fu was granted vice minister rank, placed in charge of the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue, and soon appointed vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，方開博學鴻辭科，紱所舉已眾，又以所知囑副都御史孫國璽薦舉，事聞上，上詰紱，紱自承妄言，上謂「紱乃妄舉，非止妄言，避重就輕」。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, when the erudite and eloquent examination was opened, Fu had already recommended many candidates and also entrusted men he knew to Vice Censor-in-Chief Sun Guoxuan for further recommendations. When the matter reached the emperor, he questioned Fu; Fu confessed to false statements. The emperor said: 'Fu has made false recommendations, not merely false statements—he is evading the serious and taking the light.'
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianlong reign, when the special erudite examination was opened, Fu had already recommended many candidates and also asked Vice Censor-in-Chief Sun Guoxuan to recommend men he knew. When the matter reached the emperor, he questioned Fu, who confessed to false statements. The emperor said, "Fu has made false recommendations, not merely false statements—he is evading the serious charge and pleading to the lesser."

sentences.zh: 降授詹事。

translations.literal: He was demoted and appointed tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to the post of tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 二年，以母憂歸。

translations.literal: In the second year he returned home on account of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he returned home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 六年，補光祿寺卿，遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and transferred to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and transferred to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 紱偉岸自喜。

translations.literal: Fu was imposing in stature and pleased with himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was tall and imposing and rather pleased with himself.

sentences.zh: 其論學大指，謂硃子道問學，陸九淵尊德性，不可偏廢，上聞而韙之。

translations.literal: His general view in learning was that Zhu Xi emphasized the Way of inquiry and study while Lu Jiuyuan honored moral nature, and neither could be one-sidedly abandoned. When the emperor heard this he approved it.
translations.idiomatic: His general view in scholarship was that Zhu Xi emphasized the Way of inquiry and study while Lu Jiuyuan honored moral nature, and neither could be abandoned in favor of the other. When the emperor heard this he approved.

sentences.zh: 八年，以病致仕，入辭，上問：「有欲所陳否？

translations.literal: In the eighth year he retired on account of illness; at his farewell audience the emperor asked: 'Is there anything you wish to present?'
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he retired on account of illness. At his farewell audience the emperor asked, "Is there anything you wish to say?"

sentences.zh: 」紱以慎終如始對，賜詩獎及之。

translations.literal: ' Fu answered with 'be careful at the end as at the beginning,' and the emperor bestowed a poem commending him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu answered with the phrase "be careful at the end as at the beginning," and the emperor bestowed a poem commending him.

sentences.zh: 十五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 孫友棠，乾隆十年進士，自編修累遷至工部侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandson Youtang passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of Qianlong and rose in succession from compiler to vice minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Youtang passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of Qianlong and rose in due course from compiler to vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 新昌舉人王錫侯撰字貫，坐悖逆死。

translations.literal: Xinchang provincial graduate Wang Xihou compiled the Ziguan dictionary and was executed for treasonous rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Xinchang provincial graduate Wang Xihou compiled the Ziguan dictionary and was executed for treasonous rebellion.

sentences.zh: 友棠有題詩，並奪官，賜三品卿銜。

translations.literal: Youtang had inscribed a poem on it and was also stripped of office, then granted third-rank ministerial title.
translations.idiomatic: Youtang had inscribed a poem on it and was also stripped of office, then granted a third-rank ministerial title.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 蔡珽，字若璞，漢軍正白旗人，雲貴總督毓榮子。

translations.literal: Cai Ting, styled Ruopu, was a man of the Han military Plain White Banner, son of Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Yurong.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Ting, whose style name was Ruopu, was a man of the Han military Plain White Banner and the son of Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Yurong.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十六年進士，改庶吉士，散館授檢討。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of Kangxi he became a jinshi, was made a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and upon leaving the academy was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year of the Kangxi reign he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and after leaving the academy was appointed a reviser.

sentences.zh: 洊擢少詹事，進翰林院掌院學士，兼禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to junior tutor of the heir apparent, advanced to chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, and concurrently appointed vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in due course to junior tutor of the heir apparent, then to chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, concurrently serving as vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 時世宗在潛邸，聞其能醫，欲見之，珽謝不往。

translations.literal: At the time the future Yongzheng Emperor was at the princely residence; hearing that Ting could practice medicine, he wished to see him, but Ting declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the future Yongzheng Emperor was still at his princely residence. Hearing that Ting practiced medicine, he wished to see him, but Ting declined and did not go.

sentences.zh: 六十年，四川巡撫年羹堯入覲，世​​宗命達意，仍堅辭。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year Sichuan Governor Nian Gengyao came to court for audience; the future emperor ordered him to convey his intent, but Ting still firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year Sichuan Governor Nian Gengyao came to court for audience. The future emperor ordered him to convey his intent, but Ting still firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，羹堯授川陝總督，以珽代為四川巡撫，覲聖祖熱河行在，世宗方扈從，乃詣謁而去。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year Gengyao was appointed governor-general of Sichuan-Shaanxi and Ting replaced him as governor of Sichuan. Ting had audience with the Kangxi Emperor at the Rehe imperial camp; the future emperor was then in attendance, and only then did Ting go to pay respects and depart.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year Gengyao was appointed governor-general of Sichuan-Shaanxi and Ting replaced him as governor of Sichuan. Ting had audience with the Kangxi Emperor at the Rehe imperial camp; the future emperor was then in attendance, and only then did Ting go to pay his respects and depart.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，羹堯請川、陝開採鼓鑄，珽疏言四川不產鉛，開採非便，羹堯劾珽阻撓，下部議，當奪官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng, Gengyao requested opening mining and minting in Sichuan and Shaanxi. Ting memorialized that Sichuan did not produce lead and opening mines was inadvisable. Gengyao impeached Ting for obstruction; the matter was referred to the ministry for deliberation and he should be stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yongzheng reign, Gengyao requested opening mining and minting in Sichuan and Shaanxi. Ting memorialized that Sichuan did not produce lead and that opening mines was inadvisable. Gengyao impeached Ting for obstruction; after deliberation at the ministry he was to be stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 珽辱重慶知府蔣興仁，憤自殺，珽以病卒聞，羹堯劾之，上詰責再三，始自承。

translations.literal: Ting humiliated Chongqing Prefect Jiang Xingren, who in anger killed himself. Ting reported that he had died of illness. Gengyao impeached him; the emperor questioned and rebuked him repeatedly before he finally confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Ting humiliated Chongqing Prefect Jiang Xingren, who in anger killed himself. Ting reported that he had died of illness. Gengyao impeached him; the emperor questioned and rebuked him repeatedly before he finally confessed.

sentences.zh: 下部議，擬斬，詔逮至京師，召入見，具言羹堯貪暴及所以抗拒羹堯狀，上諭曰：「珽罪應如律，然劾之者羹堯，人將謂朕以羹堯故殺珽，是羹堯得操威福柄也。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the ministry for deliberation; execution was proposed. An edict ordered him brought to the capital; he was summoned for audience and fully described Gengyao's greed and cruelty and how he had resisted Gengyao. The emperor instructed: 'Ting's crime should follow the law, yet the one who impeached him is Gengyao. People will say I am killing Ting because of Gengyao, and Gengyao would then wield the power of reward and punishment.'
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the ministry for deliberation and execution was proposed. An edict ordered him brought to the capital. He was summoned for audience and fully described Gengyao's greed and cruelty and how he had resisted him. The emperor said, "Ting's crime should follow the law, yet the one who impeached him is Gengyao. People will say I am killing Ting because of Gengyao, and Gengyao would then wield the power of reward and punishment."

sentences.zh: 其免珽罪。

translations.literal: Let Ting's crime be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Let Ting's crime be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 」特授左都御史，兼正白旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: ' He was specially appointed left censor-in-chief and concurrently commander of the Plain White Banner Han military.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially appointed left censor-in-chief and concurrently commander of the Plain White Banner Han military.

sentences.zh: 尋進兵部尚書，仍兼左都御史。

translations.literal: Soon after he was promoted to minister of war while still holding the post of left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to minister of war while retaining the post of left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 會羹堯得罪，直隸總督李維鈞隱其財產，上命珽偕內大臣馬爾賽往按，得實，奪維鈞官，以珽署總督。

translations.literal: When Gengyao fell from favor, Zhili Governor-General Li Weijun concealed his property. The emperor ordered Ting to go with inner minister Ma'ersai to investigate; the facts were established, Weijun was stripped of office, and Ting was appointed acting governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: When Gengyao fell from favor, Zhili Governor-General Li Weijun concealed his property. The emperor ordered Ting to go with inner minister Ma'ersai to investigate. The facts were established, Li Weijun was stripped of office, and Ting was appointed acting governor-general.

sentences.zh: 直隸方被水，議蠲賑，復發帑修河間、靜海諸城，俾饑民就傭受食。

translations.literal: Zhili had just suffered flooding; relief and tax exemption were deliberated, and funds were again disbursed to repair the cities of Hejian, Jinghai, and others, enabling famine victims to take employment and receive food.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili had just suffered flooding. Relief and tax exemption were deliberated, and funds were again disbursed to repair the cities of Hejian, Jinghai, and others so that famine victims could take employment and receive food.

sentences.zh: 珽奏言省會米貴，令按察使浦文倬至天津運截留漕米二萬石，以萬石運保定平糶，留萬石賑經過諸地，上如所請，敕再運通倉米十萬石往天津，加賑一月。

translations.literal: Ting memorialized that grain was dear in the provincial capital and ordered Surveillance Commissioner Pu Wenzhao to go to Tianjin to transport 20,000 shi of detained grain transport; 10,000 shi were to be transported to Baoding for sale at fair price, and 10,000 shi retained to relieve places along the route. The emperor approved as requested and ordered another 100,000 shi from the Tongcang granary transported to Tianjin, with relief extended one month.
translations.idiomatic: Ting reported that grain was dear in the provincial capital and ordered Surveillance Commissioner Pu Wenzhao to go to Tianjin to transport 20,000 shi of detained grain transport—10,000 shi to Baoding for sale at fair price and 10,000 shi to relieve places along the route. The emperor approved as requested and ordered another 100,000 shi from the Tongcang granary sent to Tianjin, with relief extended by one month.

sentences.zh: 珽奏：「請察地方官侵冒，懲胥役虛報，訪衿棍挾制，貧民戶給印券，每村給村名紙旗，以次給領。

translations.literal: Ting memorialized: 'I request investigation of local officials' embezzlement, punishment of clerks and runners for false reports, inquiry into gentry bullies who coerce, issuance of stamped certificates to poor households, and provision of village-name paper flags to each village for distribution in order.'
translations.idiomatic: Ting reported, "I request investigation of local officials' embezzlement, punishment of clerks and runners for false reports, inquiry into gentry bullies who coerce, issuance of stamped certificates to poor households, and provision of village-name paper flags to each village for orderly distribution."

sentences.zh: 賑滿，續修城工，即以賑時所給印券交驗受傭。

translations.literal: When relief ended, wall repair work would continue, and the stamped certificates issued during relief would be presented for verification to receive employment.
translations.idiomatic: When relief ended, wall repair would continue, and the stamped certificates issued during relief would be presented for verification before employment was granted."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ' This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 調補吏部尚書，仍兼領兵部、都察院及都統事。

translations.literal: He was transferred and appointed minister of personnel, still concurrently heading the ministries of war and the Censorate and the banner command.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred and appointed minister of personnel, still concurrently heading the ministries of war and the Censorate and the banner command.

sentences.zh: 四年，以珽所領事多，先後解左都御史、都統、吏部尚書，專任兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, because Ting held many concurrent posts, he was successively relieved of left censor-in-chief, banner commander, and minister of personnel, and served solely as minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, because Ting held too many concurrent posts, he was successively relieved of left censor-in-chief, banner commander, and minister of personnel, and served solely as minister of war.

sentences.zh: 旋以在直隸時徇庇昌平營參將楊雲棟，坐奪官，上命降授奉天府尹。

translations.literal: Soon after, for showing favoritism while in Zhili to Changping Garrison Assistant Regional Commander Yang Yundong, he was stripped of office; the emperor ordered him demoted and appointed prefect of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, for showing favoritism while in Zhili toward Changping Garrison Assistant Regional Commander Yang Yundong, he was stripped of office and demoted to prefect of Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 初，上以岳鍾琪代年羹堯為川陝總督，珽入對，言鍾琪叵測。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor appointed Yue Zhongqi to replace Nian Gengyao as governor-general of Sichuan-Shaanxi, Ting at audience said Zhongqi was unpredictable.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor appointed Yue Zhongqi to replace Nian Gengyao as governor-general of Sichuan-Shaanxi, Ting at audience said Zhongqi was unpredictable.

sentences.zh: 鍾琪入覲，過保定，珽方署直隸總督，造蜚語，冀以撼鍾琪。

translations.literal: When Zhongqi came to court for audience and passed through Baoding, Ting was then acting governor-general of Zhili; he spread slanderous rumors, hoping to shake Zhongqi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongqi came to court for audience and passed through Baoding, Ting was then acting governor-general of Zhili. He spread slanderous rumors, hoping to undermine Zhongqi.

sentences.zh: 事聞，上嚴旨詰責。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the emperor issued a stern edict of inquiry and rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported, the emperor issued a stern edict of inquiry and rebuke.

sentences.zh: 五年，召回京按訊，上閱羹堯幕客舉人汪景祺所著書，載珽撫四川時得夔州府知府程如絲賄，保治行第一。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was recalled to the capital for interrogation. The emperor read a book by Gengyao's client, provincial graduate Wang Jingqi, which recorded that while governing Sichuan Ting had received bribes from Kuizhou Prefect Cheng Rusi and recommended him first in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was recalled to the capital for interrogation. The emperor read a book by Gengyao's client, provincial graduate Wang Jingqi, which recorded that while governing Sichuan Ting had received bribes from Kuizhou Prefect Cheng Rusi and recommended him first in official conduct.

sentences.zh: 如絲守夔州，鬻私鹽，而捕湖廣民鬻私鹽者得輒殺之，為羹堯劾罷。

translations.literal: Rusi governed Kuizhou, sold private salt, and whenever he captured Hubei people selling private salt he killed them on the spot; Gengyao impeached and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Rusi governed Kuizhou, sold private salt himself, and whenever he captured people from Huguang selling private salt he killed them on the spot. Gengyao impeached and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 珽入對，言其冤。

translations.literal: Ting at audience said he had been wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Ting at audience said Rusi had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 上命免如絲罪，且擢為四川按察使。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Rusi's crime pardoned and moreover promoted him to Sichuan surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Rusi's crime pardoned and promoted him to Sichuan surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 至是，上頗疑景祺言。

translations.literal: At this point the emperor rather doubted Jingqi's words.
translations.idiomatic: At this point the emperor had begun to doubt Jingqi's account.

sentences.zh: 會巡撫馬會伯劾如絲營私網利疏至，命侍郎黃炳如四川按其事，以珽偕炳還奏，事實，下法司匯讞。

translations.literal: At the same time Governor Ma Huibo's memorial impeaching Rusi for private profit and netting gains arrived; the emperor ordered Vice Minister Huang Bing to go to Sichuan to investigate. Ting accompanied Bing and returned to report; the facts were established and the case was referred to the judiciary for joint sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Governor Ma Huibo's memorial impeaching Rusi for private profit arrived. The emperor ordered Vice Minister Huang Bing to go to Sichuan to investigate. Ting accompanied Bing and returned to report; the facts were established and the case was referred to the judiciary for sentencing.

sentences.zh: 尋議珽挾詐懷私，受夔關稅銀、富順縣鹽規，冒銷庫帑，並得如絲銀六萬六千、金九百，讒毀鍾琪，交結查嗣庭，凡十八事，應斬決，妻子入辛者庫，財產沒入官，命改斬監候。

translations.literal: Soon after it was deliberated that Ting had practiced deceit with private intent, received Kuiguan customs silver and Fushun County salt levies, falsely wrote off treasury funds, and altogether received from Rusi 66,000 taels of silver and 900 taels of gold, slandered Zhongqi, and associated with Zha Siting—eighteen matters in all warranting execution; wife and children to enter the Sinchi Treasury, property confiscated by the state. The emperor ordered commutation to execution after imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after it was deliberated that Ting had practiced deceit with private intent, received Kuiguan customs silver and Fushun County salt levies, falsely wrote off treasury funds, and altogether received from Rusi 66,000 taels of silver and 900 taels of gold, slandered Zhongqi, and associated with Zha Siting—eighteen counts in all warranting execution, with wife and children sent to the Sinchi Treasury and property confiscated. The emperor ordered commutation to execution after imprisonment.

sentences.zh: 六年，管理正白旗信郡王德昭又奏珽家藏硃批奏摺三件未繳進，大不敬，應立斬，詔逮至京師。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Prince of Xin De Zhao, administering the Plain White Banner, again memorialized that three vermilion-annotated memorials were found in Ting's home and not surrendered—great irreverence, warranting immediate execution. An edict ordered him brought to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Prince of Xin De Zhao, administering the Plain White Banner, again memorialized that three vermilion-annotated memorials were found in Ting's home and not surrendered—great irreverence warranting immediate execution. An edict ordered him brought to the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，珽故吏知縣黃振國坐事奪官，珽薦起河南信陽知州，巡撫田文鏡劾貪劣不法。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ting's former subordinate Magistrate Huang Zhenguo was stripped of office for an offense; Ting recommended him for appointment as prefect of Xinyang in Henan. Governor Tian Wenjing impeached him for greed, misconduct, and lawlessness.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ting's former subordinate Magistrate Huang Zhenguo had been stripped of office for an offense. Ting recommended him for appointment as prefect of Xinyang in Henan, but Governor Tian Wenjing impeached him for greed, misconduct, and lawlessness.

sentences.zh: 李紱自廣西巡撫遷直隸總督，入對，力陳振國無罪，御史謝濟世劾文鏡亦及之，言與紱合。

translations.literal: When Li Fu was transferred from governor of Guangxi to governor-general of Zhili, at audience he strongly stated Zhenguo was innocent. Censor Xie Jishi's impeachment of Wenjing also cited this, and his words matched Fu's.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Fu was transferred from governor of Guangxi to governor-general of Zhili, at audience he strongly maintained that Zhenguo was innocent. Censor Xie Jishi's impeachment of Wenjing also cited this matter, and his words matched Fu's.

sentences.zh: 上疑紱與濟世為黨，召紱還京師，戍濟世。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected Fu and Jishi were in league; he summoned Fu back to the capital and banished Jishi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected Fu and Jishi were in league; he summoned Fu back to the capital and banished Jishi.

sentences.zh: 及珽至，諭暴珽等結黨欺罔、傾陷文鏡諸罪狀，命斬振國，珽仍改斬監候，下獄。

translations.literal: When Ting arrived, the emperor announced Ting and others' crimes of forming factions, deception, and framing Wenjing, ordered Zhenguo executed, and Ting was again commuted to execution after imprisonment and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Ting arrived, the emperor announced Ting and others' crimes of forming factions, deception, and framing Wenjing, ordered Zhenguo executed, commuted Ting again to execution after imprisonment, and imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 十三年，高宗即位，赦免。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when Gaozong ascended the throne, he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, when the Qianlong Emperor ascended the throne, he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 乾隆八年，卒

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Qianlong he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Qianlong he died.

sentences.zh: 謝濟世，字石霖，廣西全州人。

translations.literal: Xie Jishi, styled Shilin, was a native of Quanzhou in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jishi, whose style name was Shilin, came from Quanzhou in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十七年，舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year of Kangxi he placed first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year of the Kangxi reign he placed first in the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，成進士，改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he became a jinshi, was made a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed a reviser.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，考選浙江道御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng he was selected by examination as censor of the Zhejiang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Yongzheng reign he was selected by examination as censor of the Zhejiang circuit.

sentences.zh: 未浹旬，疏劾河南巡撫田文鏡營私負國，貪虐不法，列舉十罪。

translations.literal: Before ten days had passed he memorialized in impeachment that Henan Governor Tian Wenjing pursued private interest against the state, was greedy, cruel, and lawless, listing ten crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Before ten days had passed he memorialized impeaching Henan Governor Tian Wenjing for pursuing private interest against the state, for greed, cruelty, and lawlessness, listing ten crimes.

sentences.zh: 上方倚文鏡，意不懌，命還濟世奏，濟世堅持不可。

translations.literal: The emperor was then relying on Wenjing and was displeased; he ordered Jishi to withdraw his memorial, but Jishi firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then relying on Wenjing and was displeased. He ordered Jishi to withdraw his memorial, but Jishi firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「文鏡秉公持正，實心治事，為督撫中所罕見者，貪贓壞法，朕保其必無，而濟世於督撫中獨劾文鏡，朕不知其何心？

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: 'Wenjing upholds justice impartially and governs affairs with sincere heart—rare among governors. Greed and corruption violating law, I guarantee he certainly has none. Yet Jishi among all governors impeaches Wenjing alone—I do not know his intent?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Wenjing upholds justice impartially and governs with a sincere heart—rare among governors. As for greed and corruption, I guarantee he has none. Yet among all governors Jishi impeaches Wenjing alone—what can his intent be?"

sentences.zh: 朕訓誡科道至再至三，誠以科道無私，方能彈劾人之有私者。

translations.literal: I have admonished the censorate again and again, truly because only when censors are without private interest can they impeach those with private interest.
translations.idiomatic: I have admonished the censorate again and again, for only when censors are without private interest can they impeach those who act from private interest.

sentences.zh: 若自恃為言官，聽人指使，顛倒是非，擾亂國政，為國法所不容。

translations.literal: If one relies on being a remonstrating official, listens to others' direction, inverts right and wrong, and disrupts state affairs, this is not tolerated by national law.
translations.idiomatic: If one relies on being a remonstrating official, listens to others' direction, inverts right and wrong, and disrupts state affairs, the law will not tolerate it.

sentences.zh: 朕豈不知誅戮諫官史書所戒？

translations.literal: Do I not know that executing remonstrating officials is what histories warn against?
translations.idiomatic: Do I not know that executing remonstrating officials is what histories warn against?

sentences.zh: 然誅戮諫官之過小，釀成人心世道之害大。

translations.literal: Yet the fault in executing remonstrating officials is small; the harm brewed to hearts and the age is great.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the fault in executing a remonstrating official is small compared with the great harm done to public morale and the moral order of the age.

sentences.zh: 禮義不愆，何卹於人言，朕豈卹此區區小節哉？

translations.literal: When ritual and righteousness are not violated, why worry about people's words? Would I worry about this petty small matter?
translations.idiomatic: When ritual and righteousness are not violated, why should I worry about what people say? Would I shrink from this petty concern?

sentences.zh: 」奪濟世官，下大學士、九卿、科道會鞫，濟世辨甚力。

translations.literal: ' Jishi was stripped of office; the case was referred to grand secretaries, Nine Chief Ministers, and censors for joint trial. Jishi argued vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: " Jishi was stripped of office, and the case was referred to the grand secretaries, Nine Chief Ministers, and censors for joint trial. Jishi argued vigorously.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書勵杜訥問：「指使何人？

translations.literal: Minister of Punishments Li Dun'e asked: 'Who directed you?'
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Punishments Li Dun'e asked, "Who directed you?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「孔、孟。

translations.literal: ' He answered: 'Confucius and Mencius.'
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Confucius and Mencius."

sentences.zh: 」問：「何故？

translations.literal: ' Asked: 'For what reason?'
translations.idiomatic: Asked, "For what reason?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「讀孔、孟書，當忠諫。

translations.literal: ' He said: 'Reading the books of Confucius and Mencius, one ought to remonstrate loyally.'
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Reading the books of Confucius and Mencius, one ought to remonstrate loyally."

sentences.zh: 見姦弗擊，非忠也！

translations.literal: Seeing wickedness and not striking at it is not loyalty!
translations.idiomatic: Seeing wickedness and not striking at it is not loyalty!"

sentences.zh: 」讞上，以濟世所言風聞無據，顯係聽人指使，要結朋黨，擬斬。

translations.literal: ' When the sentence was submitted, because Jishi's words were hearsay without basis, clearly listening to others' direction and forming factions, execution was proposed.
translations.idiomatic: When the sentence was submitted, because Jishi's charges were hearsay without basis and he had clearly acted at others' direction and formed factions, execution was proposed.

sentences.zh: 文鏡劾屬吏黃振國、邵言綸、汪諴等，李紱訟言其枉，並謂河南諸吏張球最劣，文鏡縱弗糾。

translations.literal: Wenjing impeached subordinates Huang Zhenguo, Shao Yanlun, Wang Yan, and others. Li Fu argued they were wronged and also said among Henan officials Zhang Qiu was the worst, yet Wenjing indulged him and did not impeach.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing had impeached subordinates Huang Zhenguo, Shao Yanlun, Wang Yan, and others. Li Fu argued they had been wronged and also said that among Henan officials Zhang Qiu was the worst, yet Wenjing indulged him and did not impeach him.

sentences.zh: 入對，具為上言之。

translations.literal: At audience he fully stated this to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he fully stated this to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上先入文鏡言，不直紱，而濟世罪狀文鏡又及枉振國、言綸、諴庇球諸事。

translations.literal: The emperor had first accepted Wenjing's words and did not side with Fu, yet Jishi's charges against Wenjing again cited the wrongful cases of Zhenguo, Yanlun, and Yan and shielding Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had first accepted Wenjing's account and did not side with Fu, yet Jishi's charges against Wenjing again cited the wrongful cases of Zhenguo, Yanlun, and Yan and Wenjing's shielding of Qiu.

sentences.zh: 上召大學士、九卿、科道等入見，舉前事，謂：「濟世言與紱奏一一吻合，今詰濟世劾文鏡諸事，濟世皆茫無憑據，俯首無詞，是其受人指使，情弊顯見。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned grand secretaries, Nine Chief Ministers, censors, and others for audience, cited the prior matters, and said: 'Jishi's words match Fu's memorials one by one. Now when Jishi is questioned on his impeachment of Wenjing, he has no basis for any of it and bows his head without words—clearly he was directed by others; the circumstances are obvious.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned the grand secretaries, Nine Chief Ministers, censors, and others for audience, cited the prior matters, and said, "Jishi's words match Fu's memorials point for point. Now when Jishi is questioned on his impeachment of Wenjing, he has no basis for any of it and bows his head without a word—clearly he was directed by others; the circumstances are obvious."

sentences.zh: 」命奪濟世官，往阿爾泰軍前效力贖罪。

translations.literal: ' He ordered Jishi stripped of office and sent to serve before the army in Altai to redeem his crime.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Jishi stripped of office and sent to serve before the army in Altai to redeem his crime.

sentences.zh: 濟世至軍，大將軍平郡王福彭頗敬禮之，濟世講學著書不稍輟。

translations.literal: When Jishi reached the army, Generalissimo Prince of Ping Fupeng treated him with considerable respect; Jishi lectured on learning and wrote books without the slightest pause.
translations.idiomatic: When Jishi reached the army, Generalissimo Prince of Ping Fupeng treated him with considerable respect, and Jishi continued lecturing and writing without pause.

sentences.zh: 七年，振武將軍順承郡王錫保以濟世撰古本大學注毀謗程、硃，疏劾，請治罪。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Pacifying Martial General Prince of Shuncheng Xibao, citing Jishi's commentary on the ancient text of the Great Learning slandering Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi, memorialized in impeachment and requested punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Pacifying Martial General Prince of Shuncheng Xibao, citing Jishi's commentary on the ancient text of the Great Learning as slandering Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi, memorialized in impeachment and requested punishment.

sentences.zh: 上摘「見賢而不能舉」兩節注，有「拒諫飾非，拂人之性」語，責濟世怨望謗訕，下九卿、翰詹、科道議罪。

translations.literal: The emperor excerpted the commentary on the two passages 'seeing the worthy and not being able to advance him,' which contained the words 'rejecting remonstrance, covering faults, going against human nature,' and charged Jishi with resentment and slander; the case was referred to Nine Chief Ministers, Hanlin and Hanlin bachelors, and censors for deliberation on punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor excerpted the commentary on the two passages "seeing the worthy and not being able to advance him," which contained the words "rejecting remonstrance, covering faults, going against human nature," and charged Jishi with resentment and slander. The case was referred to the Nine Chief Ministers, Hanlin academicians, and censors for deliberation on punishment.

sentences.zh: 有陸生棻者，自舉人選授江南吳縣知縣，引見，上有所詰問，不能對，改授工部主事。

translations.literal: There was one Lu Shengfen who, selected from provincial graduate, was appointed magistrate of Wuxian in Jiangnan. At audience the emperor questioned him and he could not answer; he was reassigned as principal clerk in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Lu Shengfen who, selected from among provincial graduates, was appointed magistrate of Wuxian in Jiangnan. At audience the emperor questioned him and he could not answer; he was reassigned as principal clerk in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 復引見，上見其傲慢，以其廣西人，疑與濟世為黨，命奪官發軍前，令與濟世同效力。

translations.literal: At a second audience the emperor saw he was arrogant; because he was a Guangxi man, he suspected he was in league with Jishi and ordered him stripped of office and sent to the army, commanded to serve together with Jishi.
translations.idiomatic: At a second audience the emperor found him arrogant. Because he was from Guangxi, the emperor suspected he was in league with Jishi and ordered him stripped of office and sent to the army to serve together with Jishi.

sentences.zh: 生棻撰通鑑論十七篇，錫保以為非議時政，別疏論劾。

translations.literal: Shengfen composed seventeen essays on the Comprehensive Mirror; Xibao deemed them criticizing current policy and separately memorialized in impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Shengfen composed seventeen essays on the Comprehensive Mirror. Xibao deemed them criticism of current policy and separately memorialized in impeachment.

sentences.zh: 上並下九卿、翰詹、科道議罪，尋議濟世詆訕怨望，怙惡不悛，生棻憤懣猖狂，悖逆恣肆，皆於軍前正法。

translations.literal: The emperor referred both to Nine Chief Ministers, Hanlin and Hanlin bachelors, and censors for deliberation on punishment. Soon it was deliberated that Jishi had slandered and harbored resentment without reform, and Shengfen was resentful, reckless, rebellious, and unrestrained—all to be executed before the army according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor referred both cases to the Nine Chief Ministers, Hanlin academicians, and censors for deliberation. Soon it was decided that Jishi had slandered and harbored resentment without reform, and that Shengfen was resentful, reckless, rebellious, and unrestrained—all were to be executed before the army according to law.

sentences.zh: 上密諭錫保誅生棻，縛濟世使視，生棻既就刑，宣旨釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly instructed Xibao to execute Shengfen, bound Jishi and made him watch; after Shengfen had been executed, he proclaimed an edict releasing Jishi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly instructed Xibao to execute Shengfen, bound Jishi and made him watch, and after Shengfen had been executed proclaimed an edict releasing Jishi.

sentences.zh: 濟世在戍九年，高宗即位，詔開言路，為建勳將軍欽拜草奏，請責成科道嚴不言之罰，恕妄言之罪，上嘉納焉。

translations.literal: Jishi was in exile nine years. When Gaozong ascended the throne, an edict opened the path of remonstrance. Merit-establishing General Qinbai drafted a memorial for him requesting that censors be held strictly accountable for not speaking and pardoned for speaking rashly; the emperor commended and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi was in exile nine years. When the Qianlong Emperor ascended the throne, an edict opened the path of remonstrance. Merit-establishing General Qinbai drafted a memorial for him requesting that censors be held strictly accountable for silence and pardoned for speaking rashly; the emperor commended and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 旋召濟世還京師，复補江南道御史。

translations.literal: Soon after Jishi was summoned back to the capital and reappointed censor of the Jiangnan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi was soon summoned back to the capital and reappointed censor of the Jiangnan circuit.

sentences.zh: 濟世以所撰大學注、中庸疏進上，略言：「大學注中，九卿、科道所議諷刺三語，臣已改刪，惟分章釋義，遵古本不遵程、硃，習舉業者有成規，講道學者無厲禁。

translations.literal: Jishi presented his commentary on the Great Learning and exegesis of the Doctrine of the Mean, stating briefly: 'In the Great Learning commentary, the three satirical phrases deliberated by Nine Chief Ministers and censors I have already revised and deleted. Only in dividing chapters and explaining meaning I follow the ancient text and not Cheng and Zhu. Those studying for examinations have fixed rules; those lecturing on the Way have no strict prohibition.'
translations.idiomatic: Jishi presented his commentary on the Great Learning and his exegesis of the Doctrine of the Mean, stating briefly, "In the Great Learning commentary, the three satirical phrases deliberated by the Nine Chief Ministers and censors I have already revised and deleted. Only in dividing chapters and explaining meaning I follow the ancient text rather than Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi. Those studying for examinations have fixed rules; those lecturing on the Way face no strict prohibition."

sentences.zh: 千慮一得，乞捨其瑕而取其瑜。

translations.literal: From a thousand considerations one gain—I beg to discard the flaws and take the gems.
translations.idiomatic: From a thousand considerations one may gain something—I beg that you discard the flaws and take what is valuable."

sentences.zh: 」得旨嚴飭，還其書。

translations.literal: ' He received an edict of stern admonition and his books were returned.
translations.idiomatic: He received an edict of stern admonition and his books were returned.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，濟世疏曰：「臣今所言者有二：一曰去邪勿疑，一曰出令勿貳。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong, Jishi memorialized: 'What your servant speaks of now has two points: first, remove the wicked without doubt; second, issue orders without duplicity.'
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianlong, Jishi memorialized, "What I speak of now has two points: first, remove the wicked without doubt; second, issue orders without duplicity."

sentences.zh: 有罪而復用，如程元章、哈元生者，輿論猶有恕詞；

translations.literal: Those guilty yet reemployed, such as Cheng Yuanzhang and Ha Yuansheng, still find some words of forgiveness in public opinion;
translations.idiomatic: Men who were guilty yet reemployed, such as Cheng Yuanzhang and Ha Yuansheng, still find some words of forgiveness in public opinion;

sentences.zh: 至於隆升，國人皆曰不可，猶未罷斥。

translations.literal: as for Long Sheng, the people all say he should not be used, yet he has still not been dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: but as for Long Sheng, everyone says he should not be used, yet he has still not been dismissed.

sentences.zh: 不惟不罷斥隆升而已，如王士俊以加賦為墾荒，肆毒中州，又請為田文鏡立賢良祠。

translations.literal: Not only has Long Sheng not been dismissed; men such as Wang Shijun, who treated tax increases as land reclamation and wantonly harmed the central provinces, also requested establishing a shrine of worthy and good men for Tian Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: Not only has Long Sheng not been dismissed; men such as Wang Shijun, who treated tax increases as land reclamation and wantonly harmed the central provinces, also requested establishing a shrine of worthy and good men for Tian Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 皇上既深惡之，乃調回而仍用，逮勘而復赦，乃者清問及之，議者謂將用為籓臬。

translations.literal: Your Majesty already deeply detests him, yet he was recalled and still employed; when investigated he was again pardoned; recently at imperial inquiry some said he would be used as provincial treasurer or intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty already deeply detests him, yet he was recalled and still employed; when investigated he was again pardoned; and recently at imperial inquiry some said he would be used as provincial treasurer or intendant.

sentences.zh: 籓臬總一省刑名錢穀，豈辜恩負罪之督撫所能勝任乎？

translations.literal: Treasurers and intendants oversee a province's punishments and revenue—how can a governor who has betrayed grace and bears guilt be fit for such duty?
translations.idiomatic: Treasurers and intendants oversee a province's punishments and revenue—how can a governor who has betrayed grace and bears guilt be fit for such duty?

sentences.zh: 易言渙汗，禮稱綸綍，信而已矣。

translations.literal: The Changes speak of sweat dispersing; the Rites speak of imperial edict—nothing but trust.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes speak of sweat dispersing; the Rites speak of the imperial edict—nothing matters but trust.

sentences.zh: 今則元年諭旨，二年即廢格或改易矣；

translations.literal: Now edicts of the first year are in the second year already abandoned or altered;
translations.idiomatic: Now edicts of the first year are in the second year already abandoned or altered;

sentences.zh: 特諭停止在任守制，近日督撫又漸次請行。

translations.literal: a special edict stopped mourning in office, yet recently governors have again gradually requested its implementation.
translations.idiomatic: a special edict stopped mourning while in office, yet recently governors have again gradually requested its restoration.

sentences.zh: 天下之大，何患無才？

translations.literal: The realm is vast—why worry that there are no talents?
translations.idiomatic: The realm is vast—why worry that there are no talents?

sentences.zh: 記曰'金革無闢'，又曰'君子不奪人之親'，安用此食祿忘親者為哉？

translations.literal: The Record says 'in war and emergency there is no avoidance,' and also says 'the gentleman does not deprive others of their kin'—what use are these who eat salary and forget their parents?
translations.idiomatic: The Record says, "In war and emergency there is no avoidance," and also, "The gentleman does not deprive others of their kin"—what use are men who draw salary and forget their parents?

sentences.zh: 特諭監生准入場不准考職。

translations.literal: A special edict allowed supervising students to enter the examination hall but not to take the service examination.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict allowed supervising students to enter the examination hall but barred them from the service examination.

sentences.zh: 昨世宗升祔恩詔，監生仍准考職。

translations.literal: Yesterday, in the grace edict for the Yongzheng Emperor's enshrinement, supervising students were again permitted the service examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday, in the grace edict for the Yongzheng Emperor's enshrinement, supervising students were again permitted the service examination.

sentences.zh: 考職者入仕之門，既準捐監，又准考職，復開捐例之張本也。

translations.literal: The service examination is the gateway to office; having permitted purchase of supervising student status and also permitted the service examination, this again opens the way to sale-of-office precedents.
translations.idiomatic: The service examination is the gateway to office; having permitted purchase of supervising student status and also the service examination, this again opens the door to sale-of-office precedents.

sentences.zh: 即止給虛銜，不准實授，而後命前命相違，亦不宜如此。
