translations.literal: Even if only empty titles are granted and actual appointment is not permitted, when later orders contradict earlier orders it is also inappropriate to proceed thus.
translations.idiomatic: Even if only empty titles were granted and actual appointment barred, when later orders contradict earlier ones it is still inappropriate to proceed thus.

sentences.zh: 臣聞不退不遠，大學所譏，世間君子少、小人多，已敗露者不行放流，未敗露者益無忌憚。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that not withdrawing means not going far—the Great Learning ridicules this. In the world gentlemen are few and petty men many; those already exposed are not banished, and those not yet exposed grow ever more unafraid.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that not withdrawing means not going far—the Great Learning ridicules this. In the world gentlemen are few and petty men many; those already exposed are not banished, and those not yet exposed grow ever bolder.

sentences.zh: 若發號施令，小人得以搖奪，君子無所適從，國事未有不隳者也。

translations.literal: If in issuing orders petty men can sway and overturn them and gentlemen have nowhere to turn, state affairs cannot but collapse.
translations.idiomatic: If in issuing orders petty men can sway and overturn them while gentlemen have nowhere to turn, state affairs cannot but collapse.

sentences.zh: 三年，疏言：「母蔣年七十一，行動艱難，耳目昏憒。

translations.literal: In the third year he memorialized: 'My mother Jiang is seventy-one years old, moves with difficulty, and her eyes and ears are dim and confused.'
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he memorialized, "My mother Jiang is seventy-one years old, moves with difficulty, and her eyes and ears are dim and confused."

sentences.zh: 臣欲歸養，則貧不能供甘旨；

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to return home to support her, yet is too poor to provide delicacies;
translations.idiomatic: I wish to return home to support her, yet I am too poor to provide delicacies;

sentences.zh: 欲迎養，則老不能任舟車；

translations.literal: wishes to bring her to live with him, yet she is too old to endure boat or carriage;
translations.idiomatic: I wish to bring her to live with me, yet she is too old to endure boat or carriage;

sentences.zh: 欲歸省，則往返動經半年。

translations.literal: wishes to return for a visit, yet the round trip often takes half a year.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to return for a visit, yet the round trip often takes half a year.

sentences.zh: 在家不過數月，乍逢又別，既別難逢，慈母之涕淚轉添，遊子之方寸終亂。

translations.literal: At home for no more than a few months, suddenly meeting then parting again, once parted hard to meet again—the loving mother's tears ever increase, the wanderer's heart is ever in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: At home for no more than a few months, meeting only to part again, parting only to find reunion hard—the loving mother's tears ever increase, and the wanderer's heart is ever in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 臣才不稱道府，例又從無自請遷轉。

translations.literal: Your servant's talent does not match a circuit intendant's post, and by precedent one never requests transfer on one's own.
translations.idiomatic: My talent does not match a circuit intendant's post, and by precedent one never requests transfer on one's own.

sentences.zh: 乞敕部以州縣降授湖南、廣東，量予近地，臣得母子聚首，無任哀懇。

translations.literal: I beg that the ministry be ordered to appoint me at prefectural or county rank demoted to Hunan or Guangdong, granting a place as near as possible, so your servant may reunite mother and son—I cannot bear the sorrow of this plea.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the ministry appoint me at prefectural or county rank in Hunan or Guangdong, granting a place as near as possible, so that mother and son may be reunited—I cannot bear the sorrow of this plea."

sentences.zh: 」上特授濟世湖南糧儲道。

translations.literal: ' The emperor specially appointed Jishi grain storage commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor specially appointed Jishi grain storage commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 八年，濟世聞衡陽知縣李澎徵賦縱丁役索浮費，易服偽為鄉民納賦者以往，察得實，善化知縣樊德貽與同弊，濟世詳劾。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Jishi heard that Hengyang Magistrate Li Peng in collecting taxes indulged clerks and runners in demanding extra fees. He changed clothes and disguised himself as a villager paying taxes, verified the facts, and found that Shanhua Magistrate Fan Deyi shared the same misconduct; Jishi memorialized in full impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Jishi heard that Hengyang Magistrate Li Peng, in collecting taxes, indulged clerks and runners in demanding extra fees. He changed clothes and disguised himself as a villager paying taxes, verified the facts, and found that Shanhua Magistrate Fan Deyi shared the same misconduct; Jishi memorialized a full impeachment.

sentences.zh: 巡撫許容庇德貽等，以濟世盪檢逾閒列狀入告。

translations.literal: Governor Xu Rong shielded Deyi and others and memorialized listing Jishi's licentious conduct beyond bounds.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Xu Rong shielded Deyi and the others and memorialized accusing Jishi of licentious conduct beyond bounds.

sentences.zh: 上命解任，交總督孫嘉淦會鞫，濟世捕衡陽丁役下長沙知府張琳，讞得徵收浮費有據。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him relieved of duty and referred the case to Governor-General Sun Jiagan for joint trial. Jishi arrested Hengyang clerks and runners and submitted them to Changsha Prefect Zhang Lin; sentencing established that extra fees had been collected with evidence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him relieved of duty and referred the case to Governor-General Sun Jiagan for joint trial. Jishi arrested Hengyang clerks and runners and submitted them to Changsha Prefect Zhang Lin; sentencing established that extra fees had been collected, with evidence on record.

sentences.zh: 容令岳常澧道倉德代濟世，布政使張璨附容指，貽書倉德，令更易長沙府詳牒。

translations.literal: Rong ordered Yue-Chang-Li Circuit Intendant Cang De to replace Jishi. Provincial administration commissioner Zhang Can followed Rong's direction and sent a letter to Cang De ordering him to alter the Changsha prefecture's detailed report.
translations.idiomatic: Rong ordered Yue-Chang-Li Circuit Intendant Cang De to replace Jishi. Provincial administration commissioner Zhang Can followed Rong's lead and sent a letter to Cang De ordering him to alter the Changsha prefecture's detailed report.

sentences.zh: 倉德初官給事中，嘗劾濟世奏事失儀，至是不直璨所為，發其書上嘉淦及漕運總督顧琮，嘉淦庇容，寢其事。

translations.literal: Cang De had earlier served as supervising secretary and once impeached Jishi for impropriety in memorializing. At this point he did not approve of Can's conduct, sent the letter up to Jiagan and Grain Transport Governor-General Gu Cong; Jiagan shielded Rong and shelved the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Cang De had earlier served as supervising secretary and once impeached Jishi for impropriety in memorializing. Now he did not approve of Can's conduct and sent the letter up to Jiagan and Grain Transport Governor-General Gu Cong. Jiagan shielded Rong and shelved the matter.

sentences.zh: 諭倉德委曲善處，琮諮都察院奏聞。

translations.literal: He instructed Cang De to handle the matter tactfully and harmoniously; Gu consulted the Censorate to memorial and inform the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed Cang De to handle the matter tactfully; Gu consulted the Censorate, which memorialized to inform the throne.

sentences.zh: 御史胡定糾容挾私誣劾，採湖南民謠，斥容與璨等朋謀傾濟世。

translations.literal: Censor Hu Ding impeached Rong for private motives in false impeachment, collected Hunan folk songs, and denounced Rong and Can and others for factional conspiracy to overthrow Jishi.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Hu Ding impeached Rong for acting from private motives in a false impeachment, collected Hunan folk songs, and denounced Rong and Can and others for factional conspiracy to overthrow Jishi.

sentences.zh: 上命侍郎阿里袞如湖南會嘉淦按治，而倉德以嘉淦寢其事，复揭都察院奏聞。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Vice Minister Aligun to go to Hunan and jointly investigate with Jiagan, while Cang De, because Jiagan had shelved the matter, again submitted it through the Censorate to inform the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Vice Minister Aligun to go to Hunan and jointly investigate with Jiagan. Cang De, because Jiagan had shelved the matter, again submitted it through the Censorate to inform the throne.

sentences.zh: 上責嘉淦草率扶同，召還京師，解容、璨任，奪琳、德貽、澎官。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Jiagan for carelessness and collusion, recalled him to the capital, relieved Rong and Can of duty, and stripped Lin, Deyi, and Peng of office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Jiagan for carelessness and collusion, recalled him to the capital, relieved Rong and Can of duty, and stripped Lin, Deyi, and Peng of office.

sentences.zh: 阿里袞尋奏濟世被誣劾，請復官，容、璨及按察使王玠皆坐奪官，上命並罷嘉淦，而獎倉德及定，調濟世驛鹽道。

translations.literal: Aligun soon memorialized that Jishi had been falsely impeached and requested restoration of office; Rong, Can, and surveillance commissioner Wang Jie were all stripped of office for their roles. The emperor ordered Jiagan dismissed as well, commended Cang De and Ding, and transferred Jishi to the courier and salt circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Aligun soon memorialized that Jishi had been falsely impeached and requested his restoration to office; Rong, Can, and surveillance commissioner Wang Jie were all stripped of office for their roles. The emperor ordered Jiagan dismissed as well, commended Cang De and Ding, and transferred Jishi to the courier and salt circuit.

sentences.zh: 蔣溥代為巡撫，嗛濟世密進所著書，斥為離經畔道，上曰：「朕不以語言文字罪人。

translations.literal: Jiang Pu replaced him as governor, resented Jishi's secret presentation of his own writings, and denounced them as departing from the classics and rebelling against the Way. The emperor said: 'I do not punish people for words and writing.'
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Pu replaced him as governor, resented Jishi's secret presentation of his own writings, and denounced them as departing from the classics and rebelling against the Way. The emperor said, "I do not punish people for words and writing."

sentences.zh: 」置不問。

translations.literal: ' The matter was left uninvestigated.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was left uninvestigated.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復言其老病，乃命休致。

translations.literal: Before long he again reported Jishi's old age and illness, and he was ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he again reported Jishi's old age and illness, and Jishi was ordered to retire.

sentences.zh: 歸家居十二年，卒，年六十有八。

translations.literal: He returned home and lived twelve years, then died at the age of sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home and lived twelve years, then died at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 陳學海，字志澄，江西永豐人。

translations.literal: Chen Xuehai, styled Zhicheng, was a native of Yongfeng in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xuehai, whose style name was Zhicheng, came from Yongfeng in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十二年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year of Kangxi he became a jinshi and was made a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year of the Kangxi reign he passed the jinshi examination and entered the Hanlin as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 與濟世友，授山東恩縣知縣，行取刑部主事，遷員外郎。

translations.literal: He was a friend of Jishi, was appointed magistrate of En County in Shandong, was selected for promotion to principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, and transferred to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He was a friend of Jishi, was appointed magistrate of En County in Shandong, was selected for promotion to principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, and rose to vice director.

sentences.zh: 文鏡劾振國等，上遣侍郎海壽、史貽直往按，請以學海從，得文鏡欺罔狀，將以實入告，繼乃反之，學海爭不得。

translations.literal: When Wenjing impeached Zhenguo and others, the emperor dispatched Vice Ministers Haishou and Shi Yizhi to investigate and requested that Xuehai accompany them. They obtained evidence of Wenjing's deception and were about to report the facts, but afterward reversed themselves; Xuehai argued but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenjing impeached Zhenguo and others, the emperor dispatched Vice Ministers Haishou and Shi Yizhi to investigate and requested that Xuehai accompany them. They obtained evidence of Wenjing's deception and were about to report the facts, but afterward reversed themselves; Xuehai argued but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 使還，擢御史，嘗以語濟世，濟世用是劾文鏡。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, he was promoted to censor; he once told Jishi of this, and Jishi used it to impeach Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: When the mission returned, he was promoted to censor. He once told Jishi of this, and Jishi used it to impeach Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 既譴，學海不自安，次年，以病告。

translations.literal: After the punishment Xuehai was ill at ease; the next year he reported illness.
translations.idiomatic: After the punishment Xuehai was ill at ease; the next year he reported illness.

sentences.zh: 都察院劾偽病，並及與濟世交關狀，奪官，命與濟世同效力軍前。

translations.literal: The Censorate impeached him for feigned illness and also cited his association with Jishi; he was stripped of office and ordered to serve together with Jishi before the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate impeached him for feigned illness and also cited his association with Jishi; he was stripped of office and ordered to serve together with Jishi before the army.

sentences.zh: 雍正七年，召還，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongzheng he was recalled and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Yongzheng reign he was recalled and appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：田文鏡與鄂爾泰、李衛同為世宗所激賞。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Tian Wenjing, along with Ortai and Li Wei, were alike highly commended by the Yongzheng Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Tian Wenjing, along with Ortai and Li Wei, were alike highly commended by the Yongzheng Emperor.

sentences.zh: 高宗謂三人者文鏡為​​最下，允哉！

translations.literal: Gaozong said that among the three Wenjing was the lowest—indeed!
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor said that among the three Wenjing was the lowest—indeed!

sentences.zh: 文鏡馭屬吏苛急，待士尤虐。

translations.literal: Wenjing governed subordinates harshly and urgently and treated scholars with especial cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing governed subordinates harshly and treated scholars with especial cruelty.

sentences.zh: 紱固以好士得時譽，宜其惡之深，而所爭以為枉者，為珽所薦吏。

translations.literal: Fu had indeed won contemporary reputation for loving scholars; it is fitting that he hated Wenjing deeply, yet those he contended were wronged were subordinates recommended by Ting.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had indeed won contemporary reputation for loving scholars; it is fitting that he hated Wenjing deeply, yet those he contended were wronged were subordinates recommended by Ting.

sentences.zh: 濟世又繼以為言，世宗疑珽使紱入告，不納；

translations.literal: Jishi again followed in speaking of this; the Yongzheng Emperor suspected Ting had made Fu report to the throne and did not accept it;
translations.idiomatic: Jishi again followed in speaking of this; the Yongzheng Emperor suspected Ting had made Fu report to the throne and did not accept it;

sentences.zh: 又嗾濟世露章論劾，互相結，務欲傾文鏡。

translations.literal: he also incited Jishi to open memorial impeachment, they formed factions with each other, determined to overthrow Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: he also incited Jishi to lodge open memorial impeachments; they formed factions with each other, determined to overthrow Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 獄遂不可解，然終未即誅死。

translations.literal: The cases thus could not be resolved, yet in the end they were not immediately executed.
translations.idiomatic: The cases thus could not be resolved, yet in the end they were not immediately executed.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣服，諸人皆得湔祓，紱復起，濟世亦見用。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, all were able to be cleansed; Fu was restored, and Jishi was also employed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianlong Emperor succeeded to the throne, all were able to be cleansed; Fu was restored, and Jishi was also employed.

sentences.zh: 孰謂世宗嚴？

translations.literal: Who says the Yongzheng Emperor was severe?
translations.idiomatic: Who says the Yongzheng Emperor was severe?

sentences.zh: 不肯戮諫臣，固明言之矣。

translations.literal: His refusal to execute remonstrating ministers he stated clearly enough.
translations.idiomatic: His refusal to execute remonstrating ministers he stated clearly enough.
